caption: What if you lived in a spinning space city? In orbit you float, and astronauts lose about 1-1.5% of their bone density every month. The fix is spin. In 1974, physicist Gerard O'Neill designed giant rotating habitats. His biggest is a tube about 32 km long (almost six Bandra-Worli Sea Links) and 6-8 km wide. Turning about once every 2 minutes pushes you onto the floor with Earth-like gravity, while the floor races along at over 600 km/h. Look up and you'd see houses on the 'ceiling', kilometres away. Climb toward the middle and you get lighter, until you float at the centre. Spin also bends falling things, so a dropped ladoo lands slightly off target. India's Bharatiya Antariksh Station targets its first module by 2028, with no spin. Plot twist: Earth's equator spins at about 1,670 km/h, yet that makes you only about 0.3% lighter. Would YOU move to a space city? 👇
